title: Galapagos corals suggest climate change drives stronger El Niños | New Scientist
description: Coral records from the Galapagos Islands indicate El Niños have been gathering strength over the past 40 years, in line with rising global temperatures
author: Madeleine Cuff

title: Astonishing whale feeding frenzy seen off the eastern coast of Greenland | New Scientist
description: The population of baleen whales along eastern Greenland has boomed in recent decades, and reporter Leah Crane recounts a profound experience of seeing them
author: Leah Crane

title: Octopuses released into Adriatic Sea to tackle invasive crabs | New Scientist
description: Atlantic blue crabs have moved into the Mediterranean and Adriatic seas, where they are a problem both for ecosystems and local economies, but octopuses might offer a solution
author: Alessio Cozzolino

title: Exercise may create new neurons by making other brain cells contract | New Scientist
description: Physical activity causes a type of brain cell called astrocytes to contract, which then leads to the formation of new neurons, according to a study in mice
author: Helen Thomson

title: Driving data can predict crash black spots before accidents happen | New Scientist
description: An analysis of data collected from hundreds of thousands of cars in Australia offers an insight into driving behaviour that can be used to identify sections of road where crashes may occur in the future
author: James Woodford

title: Huge progress made in attempt to upgrade standard model of particles | New Scientist
description: A challenging mathematical effort undertaken by a team of undergraduates has put bounds on a promising set of ways to break and upgrade the standard model of particle physics
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan
